prompt: Accept a phone number in exactly two shapes -- "(212) 555-0199" or "212-555-0199" -- and separately strip a number down to its digits. Nulls must not blow up.
explanation: Grouping the two prefixes as (\(\d{3}\) |\d{3}-) lets one pattern describe both layouts while the shared 555-0199 tail is written once. Parentheses are metacharacters, so the literal ones in the area code have to be escaped as \( and \), which in a Java string means typing a doubled backslash. Because matches() requires the entire string to match, a valid number embedded in a sentence is correctly rejected without any extra anchoring.
hints: \d{3} means exactly three digits; {4} at the end pins the line number length so 019 and 01999 both fail.
Put the two prefixes in a group separated by | and note that one of them ends with a space character.
digitsOnly is a single replaceAll with the negated class [^0-9] and an empty replacement.
